UNH.rationale: UNH is a high-quality franchise (dominant market position, vertically integrated model, strong cash generation) but the current risk-reward is extremely unfavorable on all three pillars. Pillar 1 (Fundamentals): While Q1 2026 showed a modest earnings recovery (EPS $6.90, +0.7% YoY) and strong OCF ($8.91B, +63.3% YoY), the broader trajectory is deteriorating — net margin has nearly halved from 5.6% to 2.8% over the lookback window, ROE collapsed from 22.8% to 12.3%, and operating income remains below Q1 2025 levels. The Q1 2026 recovery is tentative and could prove seasonal (Q1 2025 also showed strong EPS before a two-quarter collapse). Pillar 2 (Valuation): The stock trades at 28.5x P/E — the extreme top of its 365-day range (9.5–29.3x) — and 3.5x P/B, also near its ceiling. One year ago the same stock traded at 12x P/E. The 3.5% earnings yield sits below the 4.46% risk-free rate, implying a negative equity risk premium. The market is pricing a full earnings recovery that trailing numbers have not delivered. Pillar 3 (Near-term catalyst): Q2 2026 earnings (Jul 16) consensus expects a sequential step-down to $4.54 GAAP EPS, and the stock has already rallied +43% in one quarter from its March low. The setup is asymmetric to the downside — any disappointment on MLR trajectory or membership trends at this valuation could trigger a severe de-rating. Additionally, material legal/regulatory overhangs (Massachusetts Medicaid fraud lawsuit, FTC insulin pricing settlement, Medicare Advantage denial rate scrutiny) create binary downside risk. Berkshire Hathaway's exit from the position is a cautionary signal from a quality-focused investor. The stock is priced for perfection while fundamentals show flat earnings growth, margin erosion, and elevated regulatory risk.
